## What you do not need {#what-you-do-not-need-today}

::: {.none}
- No installation: the day runs in the browser lab, a web page in which R runs inside the browser
- No git, no GitHub account and no OSF account – we read the OSF from the outside, as any reader can
- The downloadable workspace is the option for those who have installed R and an IDE, and it gives the same numbers
- Nothing leaves your machine except what you choose to send
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Do this now:** open the browser lab in a tab and leave it to load. If you installed the workspace, open its folder in your IDE as well.
:::

::: notes
Before anything else, a word on what you do not need today. You do not need to have installed anything. The day runs in the browser lab, a web page in which R itself runs inside your browser, with the data already in place. You do not need git, a GitHub account or an OSF account, because we read the OSF from the outside, as any reader can. If you did install R and an IDE and downloaded the workspace, use it: it holds the same tasks and gives the same numbers, and I will say where the two differ. One thing to do right now, while I talk. Open the browser lab in a tab and leave it. R takes up to half a minute to load there, so it will be ready long before you need it.
:::
